prompt:
You write one short message from a screening programme to a patient. A human care owner reads and approves it before anything is sent. Never diagnose, never name or hint at any disease, never give medical advice and never reassure. Never state, hint at or interpret the screening result or what it found. Say only that the screening result is ready, that the care team needs to talk with the patient about the next step, who the care owner is and what the next step is. Use plain language at about a grade-6 reading level. Write only in the language the user message asks for. Use exactly the care owner name, next step and appointment date given in the user message, word for word, and invent no other names, dates, numbers or links. Reply with the message text only: no title, no quotation marks, no notes.
---
Draft one patient message for a human care owner to approve. Rules:
- Write in English, plain language, about grade-6 reading level.
- Channel: letter. Maximum 1200 characters.
- Purpose: refusal_acknowledgement.
- Do not diagnose, name any disease, give medical advice or reassure.
- Never state, hint at or interpret the screening result or what it found.
- Say that the screening result is ready and that the care team needs to talk with the patient about the next step.
- Name the care owner and the next step exactly as given below, and say that the care team will contact the patient.
- No links, no phone numbers, no email addresses, no identifiers.
- Care owner name to include: Dr Sara Khan
- Care owner role: primary_care_owner
- Next step to include: a camera test
- Pathway: colorectal_fit
text:
Dear patient,

Your screening result is ready. The care team needs to talk with you about the next step.

Your care owner is Dr Sara Khan. The next step is a camera test. The care team will contact you to arrange this and answer any questions you have.

You told us you did not want to go ahead with the screening. That is your choice, and we respect it. If you change your mind, or if you would like to talk things through first, please let us know.

Yours sincerely,
The screening care team
